courses.name: Applications of R for Data Science
courses.description: Intended to prepare students for subsequent courses requiring computation with R, providing powerful and easy to use tools for statistical data analysis. Covers basics of R and R Studio including file handling, data simulation, graphical displays, vector and function operations, probability distributions, and inferential techniques for data analysis.
courses.prerequisite_text: DATA100, STAT100, MATH135, or any 400-level STAT course.

courses.name: Experiential Learning
courses.prerequisite_text: Must have learning proposal approved by the CMNS-Mathematics Department.

courses.name: Applied Probability and Statistics II
courses.description: Point estimation - unbiased and consistent estimators. Interval estimation. Minimum variance and maximum likelihood estimators. Testing of hypotheses. Regression, correlation and analysis of variance. Sampling distributions. Elements of non-parametric methods.
courses.prerequisite_text: 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (STAT400, STAT410).

courses.name: Probability Models
courses.description: Random variables, Joint Distributions, Hierarchical Models, Random Samples, Algorithms for generating samples, Markov Chains, Poisson Processes, Stochastic Processes, Simulations.
courses.prerequisite_text: Minimum grade of C- in STAT400 or STAT410.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science and Machine Learning
courses.description: An introductory course to the recent developments in the fields of data science and machine learning. Emphasis will be given to mathematical and statistical understanding of commonly used methods and processes.
courses.prerequisite_text: Minimum grade of C- in MATH241 or MATH340; and minimum grade of C- in MATH240,  MATH461 or MATH341;  and minimum grade of C- in STAT400 or STAT410;  students who have taken courses with content comparable to STAT400/410 may request permission of the instructor.

courses.name: Introduction to Statistical Computing with SAS
courses.description: Descriptive and inferential statistics. SAS software: numerical and graphical data summaries; merging, sorting and splitting data sets. Least squares, regression, graphics and informal diagnostics, interpreting results. Categorical data, lifetime data, time series. Applications to engineering, life science, business and social science.
courses.prerequisite_text: 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (STAT400, STAT410); and must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in STAT401 or STAT420; students who do not meet the STAT401 or STAT420 requirement but who have taken a statistics course may contact the math department to confirm eligibility.

courses.name: Sampling Theory
courses.description: Simple random sampling. Sampling for proportions. Estimation of sample size. Sampling with varying probabilities. Sampling: stratified, systematic, cluster, double, sequential, incomplete.
courses.prerequisite_text: 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (STAT401, STAT420).

courses.name: Introduction to Biostatistics
courses.description: Probabilistic models. Sampling. Some applications of probability in genetics. Experimental designs. Estimation of effects of treatments. Comparative experiments. Fisher-Irwin test. Wilcoxon tests for paired comparisons.
courses.prerequisite_text: 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (MATH120, MATH136, or MATH140);.

courses.name: Actuarial Mathematics
courses.description: Major mathematical ideas involved in calculation of life insurance premiums, including compound interest and present valuation of future income streams; probability distribution and expected values derived from life tables; the interpolation of probability distributions from values estimated at one-year multiples; the 'Law of Large Numbers' describing the regular probabilistic behavior of large populations of independent individuals; and the detailed calculation of expected present values arising in insurance problems.
courses.prerequisite_text: 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (STAT400 or STAT410); and 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (MATH340, MATH241).
